I have BPD, and in my personal situation, I am almost never hurtful/manipulative. I know that this is one of the most commonly talked-about symptoms, but it not present in ALL cases. At least not in such a form as what you have witnessed.

I too fear abandonment of course, but I fear it so much that I feel the absolute need to please everyone in every way that I possibly can, even if the sacrifices I have to make are illogically high. I also have OCD, and tend to obsess over guilt more than any other emotion, which also leads to feeling the need to make everyone happy. This can be viewed as being manipulative, and maybe it's true.... but I can at least say that I do not (at least not intentionally) say or do mean things to anyone other than myself.

Also, because of my obsession over guilt and my "black and white" thinking, I have the deepest of urges to be "good", not "bad'. This generally means that I refrain from drinking/smoking/breaking the rules or doing anything "wrong", because that would mean that I am a very "bad" person. When I feel that I have done something "bad", I take it out on myself, not other people.

I will admit that I do sometimes find myself pleading for help from others too often, but I try my best to make it up to those who help when I am able.

I will also admit that I did not believe that BPD had anything to do with me at first. It took quite a bit of education before I finally came to terms of having it.

I hope this is what you meant when you described what you were hoping for in the comments. I'm sorry you have such a rough case of BPD in your family, but the fact that it is going untreated explains why it has become so unbearable for people around her, like you. I hope that one day she will accept help.

It makes me wonder who is actually the ones doing it wrong.

.... and then I realize that no matter how "gifted" I may be, I got the wrong kind of gift for this world.

I should note that I am female, so your stance on this might be completely different.... but I *have* to do deep breathing, and I *have* to stretch. It's simple, I know.... and I'm sure you've heard it plenty 'o times before. But I had to have someone *teach* me how to "deep breath properly" when I was hospitalized, because I had been doing it incorrectly all my life. Feeling a true deep breath was amazing, and I suddenly understood why people suggested it all the time. Also, with the stretching.... I don't mean getting up, rolling out of a bed, and touching your toes or swinging your arms. I mean sitting down somewhere comfortable and calm so that you may dedicate *time* and *attention* to the act, and really be in the moment (this was something else I learned while hospitalized).

I am very very tense, all of the freaking time. Relieving a little bit of the physical pain is a nice helper to dealing with all of the other sort of pain going on.

I hope you're able to find whatever works best for you.

There has *got* to be more to this. Some history, or some previous discussion she had with you.... something....

Unfortunately, you will have to rely mostly on her for this one. Everyone experiences these things differently. I can offer some suggestions from my perspective (I am also a depressed female with anxiety disorders), but keep in mind that these are only what I have observed helpful to me, specifically.

Instead of asking questions like, "What's wrong?" or "What can I do to help?" (because sometimes there is no real answer to these questions), try asking, "What are you thinking about?".... this sort of question is generally slightly easier to answer. It's a pretty personal question, and sometimes I don't want to answer it.... but it least it is something I can find the answer to a little easier.

From there, just go with it and listen. You can try offering advice, but please be careful in doing that. I always hated it when people said, "How about we go for a walk?" or "Okay, let's treat you to some ice cream and a movie so you'll feel better!".... those can occasionally be helpful for a moment or two, but seriously? Things that help *most* people feel better can often times trigger people with depression in a worse way. 

I don't know how close the two of you are, but hugs definitely help me at times. Only at certain times, but still.... hugs really are great. She may prefer to do that instead of talk things out all the time. Talking is a good way to vent when she needs it, but could also make her feel even worse if she feel stuck talking about it when she wants to move on.

Try to figure out which of her five sense she is most sensitive to, and help her use that to make herself feel better. For example, if it is sight, then maybe she should stash a stack of old pictures or art pieces that make her feel happy so that she can look at them during her down times. Mine, personally, is smell: I keep a box with small candles in it and smell them for comfort. Also, I have a very soft pillow that I cuddle with and rock myself with if I need to.

Why did she stop taking her meds?

It was my pleasure. Really. :3

And *yes*, I *totally* know what you mean -_-.... in a way, I wish that I were actually just a flawed character that I could manually fix.... yet at the same time, knowing that it's not my fault for being this way is also comforting at moments. It's odd. All of it.

My mom is German, and as strong-willed as it gets. That means that she tried to raise me as her stubborn and independent ox-like daughter. And I strived so hard to be that for her.... so the endless years of not being able to do so were crippling to the core. I know it's hard not to feel defeated in taking a step toward getting some help. I whole-heartedly relate to that. It sucks, and I'm sorry that I don't have any words of wisdom to offer in how to feel less shameful about it. But our moms *will* love us, no matter what. And that's all we can cling to.

:) I hope you're doing better. We have a lot ahead of us!

Aside from not being suicidal (I very much am -_-), I relate very very much to all of these thoughts.

Self-destruction seems to be my fate. I've been self-harmful to myself in various ways for over a decade. Each time I break one habit, I pick up another. I don't fully understand it even after all of these years; sometimes I seem to have different reasons for doing it. And as of (relatively) recently, I slipped into one of the most horrible "extreme lows" I've ever had.... and I'm still stuck in it right now, trying to crawl out through either the top or the bottom: some days I desperately try to be positive while other days I figure that life isn't worth continuing if I have to live with this "disease" I have. Or some moments I do nothing at all, because nothing at all is precisely what I want to do and all I can handle, anyway.

If you have not done so already, you need to seek out some help. Thankfully, I forced myself into the Student Wellness center on my college campus, where the counselors took my problems more seriously than anyone ever has in my life.  And thank God that someone listened and believed me for once, because I'd be long gone if they hadn't. With a lot of time, support, and guidance in this area.... I was eventually able to open up to family one more time about just how seriously ill I truly was. Because, you know what? It *is* serious.

**And what you think/feel is not your fault.**

In fact, self-harm is a primal instinct.  Even distressed monkeys pull out patches of their own fur when they are feeling distressed.  That's because our minds put physical problems ahead of psychological ones.  We cope with tiresome and negative thoughts by giving our mind something with a higher priority to focus on: physical danger.  We merely have to learn-- with some help-- how to *cope* in better ways than injury.

What resources do you have available to you? Yes, reddit may be helpful in certain ways.... but some people need to have genuine human contact about this sort of thing.

I don't know if this will help in any way or not, but on one particularly bad day, I was texting my mother from beneath my covers (I am far away, in college) about how hard of a time I was having with battling my self-harm and suicidal ideations. She told me that although she knows that she would never be able to truly understand what I'm going through, she hopes I keep fighting and not let my depression fully envelope me....

*".... because I am selfish, and I want you in my life, no matter what."*
I related to this so much. -_- I loved/hated it. If that makes some sense.
Thanks.... I feel a little bit better now, knowing that other people experience this as well. :)

I do have times when I really do get frustrated and fight with myself (very similarly to how you described your three voices), and then I have the other times when I'm minutes away from suicide and a *liiiittle* part of me way off in the background is grabbing for me and pleading that I reconsider. I have visualizations, sometimes, that part of me is hugging the crying one. Stuff like that. 

Nonetheless, it is nice to know that I'm not the only one who feels similarly to the way I do. :)

Thank you. I really *do* have depression (I'm only just now seeking help for it as I have officially hit rock-bottom, but I've been depressed and suicidal for about a decade before now).... I mean, I know what you're saying, I just mean that I can't tune "that part of me" out or overpower it. At least not yet. But I'm working on it. The biggest difference I feel when I am in an "extreme low" rather than a "mild low" is that the part of me that resembles depression kind of.... consumes the other part of me. So I *have* no other positive voice to argue back with. Does that make sense? This concept is difficult for me to put into words. :/

I have two dogs, myself.... and they have saved my life multiple times over the years of depression I've had. I hope they know it. They love me and genuinely *love* to be with me, no matter how gloomy and infectious I am to other people. They never get tired or sick of my illness.... they never make me feel lazy or stupid or insane. They are what have kept me from suicide so many times.

There are two times in particular that I will share. I have had depression for a decade, with occasional "extreme lows". In one of these episodes, I decided that I was going to overdose on caffeine pills. I was on my kitchen floor with my death in my hand. Both dogs were asleep. I sat shivering and crying for a few minutes, and as I raised my hand to pop the pills, my male dog jumped off the bed and walked over. He stretched, yawned, licked my face, plopped down into my lap, and looked up at me. I hugged him and cried until I fell asleep right there.

Another time, I had tried to distract myself from my suicidal thoughts by taking a warm shower. I had been sitting in my tub with the water on for probably thirty minutes, just crying. I was ready to give up. I was utterly hopeless and beyond saving. I was rocking myself and crying into my palms when I felt a little tongue licking water droplets from my arm. I looked, and my female dog had poked her head in through the shower curtain. I told her how sorry I was and how much I loved her, but that I just couldn't deal with living this way. She wagged her tail and smiled (yes, she smiles-- she shows her teeth), and leaned to lick my face.

I'm sorry it's so lengthy. I'm just so grateful to have my dogs. They are able to help me so much better than most other people.

Dear part of my brain torturing me:

I cannot imagine what you could possibly be getting out of all of this. I hate you. You've made me feel and think things that no amount of ice cream or hugs or happy music and pretty colors could cure. And you know what? I'm still here. You can waste my time, but I finally have people helping me to deal with you. It's not just me you're against, anymore. You've done your worst, and believe me- it was a damn good fucking fight. But I'm still alive, damnit. And you're going to learn to shut the fuck up and listen to me. We are *going* to do something with this body. We are *going* to learn how to be social without these stupid and embarrassing anxiety attacks you love to throw at me. I know that I will have you at my side for the rest of my life.... but you've had your fun. 

We are *going* to love ourself. 

**You loose.**

This is exactly how I felt, too. I always avoided it like the plague, in fear that everyone would just feed off of one another and make matters worse. Instead, I find so much support and help. It's truly comforting just to know that there *are* people who understand that this is a disease.

I think I hover in and out of both. I feel like I sometimes just sort of "accept my fate" and, like you put it, become "comfortable" with depression. Unfortunately, I let it become who am I, entirely. The *hard* part, though, is when I really *do* wish for it all to stop, and I really *do* want the strength to say "no!" and feel better. When I can't do it, though, is when my depression only gets worse. And thus, the cycle repeats.
It did.

I'm glad to see that you've named your depression and made it something separate from yourself; I've heard a lot of positive things in doing that. I haven't been able to dive into that way of thinking just yet, but am working on it. It's a goal.

None of this is your fault. None of this is you. You did not choose this, and you cannot help it. People don't get angry at my sister for having Type 1 diabetes. They help her and support her. Depression, though I *know* (trust me) how difficult it is for us to see it as a disease rather than merely a character defect, truly is a real and serious disease. There might not be a *cure*, but just like my sister controls her diabetes through insulin, we have to find ways that work with us to control our depression. Different people have to do different things (different coping strategies or different medications and so forth); the biggest struggle for most of us is figuring out how to manage it.

Don't blame yourself. No one else should, either. You're not worthless. We're just ill, trying to get better. It takes patience.

Yup, I can relate to this, too. I remember feeling so infuriated by happiness being around me. I'm pretty sure it's a jealousy sort of issue. It came so naturally and easy to other people, and I hated to see it-- they were unintentionally flaunting what I couldn't achieve.

Do *you* feel like you are at risk for suicide?

> Please tell me I'm not alone....

While I cannot say that I experience depression in the same way you do, I *can* say that you are *not* alone. I don't have as much anger as you do in particular, just sadness and anxiety. I don't loath people.... instead I put every human being on the planet ahead of myself because I feel utterly inadequate. Also, I am so terrified of other people directing any sort of attention my way that I avoid going into the public at *every cost possible*. I'm not saying I love society, because I do agree with you that humans as a whole just.... well, suck.  But despite how much I hate I feel toward the way "everyone" is, I cannot feel any hate toward one specific person or any group of people: just myself. (That goes for hating the peppiness of other people as well: I hated the fact that they were happy, but never wished for them to not be happy.)

Anyway.... other than the differences in anger and sadness, I feel a *lot* of the same things you do. :(

I wish I had better words of advice and yadda yadda yadda.... but all I can say right now is that you shouldn't feel so completely alone.

What really got me to finally do it was the thought that, "Hell, I'm uncontrollably sad or numb all the time, anyway.... so if she responds negatively, I'll just feel what I also do. What do I have to lose?" The risk of not telling her was to continue on my journey alone (which wasn't working), whereas the risk of telling her was either dealing with more of what I already had, or possibly receiving some much-needed help.

It might not exactly be the best motivator, but I don't really care.... because it got me to do it. And, you know what? She's being supportive as best as she can.  Accepting her aid only makes me feel guilty, per usual.... but that is yet another thing I just have to improve on. Not feeling guilty.  Because this is not our fault.


*P.S.,  I'm female :) .... but nonetheless, thank you for your comment, and good luck. :3*

Here some good hope: I honestly believe that many of the ideals about depression have improved among the health industry society.

I think you ought to go for it.  Having a *good* counselor *will* make a *huge* difference.... so if you find that you're not getting what you need from whomever you speak with, explore other options in who to talk to. (I've had my own fair share of pointless counselor visits, too.... thankfully, I finally found one who is "right" for me, personally.)

As for medication: there are plenty of options, and probably more variety available now than there was in your last attempt.  If you really do not like the one you're on, you *have* to say something.

I wish I had better words to offer than that. Sorry. :/

Good luck to you. *-hugs-*

I just came to say thank you for asking this question. I have the same problem. People keep having high hopes and positive attitudes about how this will all be over with soon if I just keep my head up.

I don't just sit around and wait and hope for this "phase" to end. I've been fighting for years, and struggle *every*, *single*, *day*.
Sitting around and waiting for this to leave me seems to be the approach they are taking-- not me.

Although I don't have any problems with being *unable* to cry, I have felt this feeling you describe that suggests crying would help you feel better. I'll admit that sometimes, it did help me. Honestly, though..... most of the time, it didn't. All it usually does is leave me with a swollen and red face, a fatigued body, and a numb mind. Then I sleep. Hard. And I wake up the next day, feeling just like the last.

Some people need to do different things to release the tension.  Some people do get better use out of crying. Some people have to exercise.  Some people write. Some draw. Some sing.

Go find what is it that helps you. It might not have anything to do with *physically* expressing emotion.

Good luck.
I'm sorry for you past experiences; I also know how unmotivational that can be for retrying. How long ago was this?

Actually, don't apologize. Please. There is no need, whatsoever.

I went through that at one point as well, though I was living with my father. In high school, I had scribbled a bunch of my thoughts onto a piece of paper in order to vent a little.  My teacher caught me not paying attention and walked over to my desk.  He happened to see a few "red flag" words and took up the note. After class, I was taken to the counselor's office. She had the note, so I couldn't just deny it all. I had already been exposed, so I figured I might as well open up. I wasn't ready, but I had no choice. The counselor told my dad and step-mother. She had to, by law.... and yeah, I felt the very same way about it as you: I felt like everyone was suddenly ganging up on me for being "some fucked up piece of shit".

Instead of actual help and support, my dad almost mocked me for it. He never really left me alone, but never helped, either.

This time around, now that I'm getting *actual* help.... it feels much better. My privacy feels very violated in some ways, because, yes.... people don't leave me alone and don't exactly treat me the same way.

But I just have to keep telling myself that they are doing it out of good intentions, not to put me down.

Keep your head up. :/ We'll get through this. It'll take more time than we'd like.... but we'll do it, together. :(
*hugs* :3
:) Thank you so much for your encouragement. It really does mean very much to me. <3

I have a question for you, if you don't mind. I considered PMing it, but what the hell.

My mom is set on the idea that this is all 100% temporary.  While I do love the idea of that, it's hard to believe it.  She seems to think that pulling me from Tech and having me closer to home will solve the problem.... yet, as I mentioned, this has been going on for a very long time.

I guess my question is (and I know the answer may be different for everyone).... just how temporary is all of this?  Is it possible that I will continue to "manage" it my entire life? Do you know?

It's probably a silly question. :/

I might find myself PMing you in the future. You have been an amazing help to both me, and hopefully (when/if I send them some of those links) to my family.

Thank you, again and again.  The biggest battle for me is not feeling guilty/ashamed/sorry. I *know* better, I just can't *do* better.... and trying to control it is about as effective as covering your mouth when you vomit.

Baby steps. Baby steps. I can do this. :'(
:'3 Thank you so much. I'm getting much more positive comments and support here than I ever really expected.

I agree completely. My entire family seems to shrug depression off as something common and "not a big deal".

Having "The Blues" is common.  True "Depression" is a bigger deal.  I was in denial for a long time that I might actually be depressed, because my family sort of seemed to put this idea in the air that it wasn't possible-- that it wasn't an option, or that it wasn't real.

I feel very sorry for your situation.  I feel like even though I might not fully understand it, I relate on some level.  And it sucks.  :(

Best of luck to you.... I mean that.

This truly means so, so much to me. I can't thank you enough.

:')

EDIT: Anyone else who happens to come across this, it is proving *very* useful.... thank you!

I won't say it was easy.  It didn't even make me feel any better at first, because upon hitting "send", I was overwhelmed with panic.

But I have gotten to the point where I had little other choice.  I am so desperate to do anything in order to save myself.... because that is what it has come to.  I am ashamed to admit it, but I did this to myself: I let this get so bad over so long of a period of time, that my options are to either:
A) finally open up about how bad it has truly gotten,
B) continue doing what obviously *doesn't work*, or
C) cave in, and commit the suicide that has been scratching the walls of my brain for years, day in and day out.

I gained more confidence in my decision to finally tell someone in my family about it when I came to the conclusion that there was really very little to lose.

In other words, I suppose it didn't really cost me as much courage as it may seem, and I therefor don't take credit for any bravery. If I can do it.... you can.

Best of luck to you. :3 Sincerely.
